title: Karmic tail 3-13-10 in the destiny matrix: prune, don’t uproot

seo.title: 3 13 10 in the destiny matrix: a karmic tail without scare stories
seo.description: Tail 3-13-10: the Empress, Death and the Wheel. Why the “suicide” label is wrong, who has this tail, every birth date with it, and how to work with it.

short: The karmic tail 3-13-10 is the scenario of a gardener who grows living things generously, but at the first change of season doesn’t prune them — he pulls them up by the roots. The Empress at the entry (M) gives the desire to create, Death in the middle (N) turns every transition into a final ending, and the Wheel of Fortune at the root (D) teaches you to pass through a change of phase without losing the harvest. This is not a “suicide programme”, as popular lists frighteningly call this tail: it is about how a person ends projects and relationships, not about the end of life. The tail is rare — 149 birth dates since 1900 — and it always comes with the centre 20, Judgement.

paragraphs: If you boil it down to one thought: Death in this tail is not a misfortune that befalls what was created, but the habitual way a person closes stages themselves. Working through the tail does not mean you stop ending things. It teaches you to end a part, not the whole.

sections.h2: Why 3-13-10 is called “Suicide”, and what is wrong with that label
paragraphs: In popular lists, the 3-13-10 tail is labelled “Suicide” or “the Suicide”. Then usually come stories about a soul that “failed to cope in a past life”, about a weak instinct for self-preservation and a choice “between life and death”. The label is put together mechanically: the Empress is life, Death is death, the Wheel is fate, so the total is “a life cut short by one’s own hand”. If you have come here after such a reading — especially a reading of your child’s chart — breathe out. This conclusion does not follow from the arcana themselves.

In The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Arthur Edward Waite writes of the thirteenth card as change of form and passage “from lower to higher”. On his horseman’s banner is the Mystic Rose, “which signifies life”, and between the pillars on the horizon shines “the sun of immortality”. He finds the existing explanations of the card better than usual on the whole: “rebirth, creation, destination, renewal”. Waite does not strike the theme of death out of the card, but neither his book nor Benebell Wen’s modern Holistic Tarot gives any grounds for predicting death or misfortune from the arcanum. And a karmic tail in the Arcana Sense scheme does not assign events at all: it describes a habitual pattern that repeats.

The frightening label does have an honest grain of truth, and it is worth naming directly. This scenario has a difficult place — the pause between the end of one form and the start of the next. The old is already over, the new not yet planted, and the empty field can feel heavy: “I don’t feel like doing anything”, “it was all for nothing”. This is not a sentence and not a character trait but a phase, discussed in detail below.

If thoughts of death are not a symbol from the matrix but something that is happening to you or someone close to you right now, you need to talk to a living person, not to the arcana. Call your local emergency number or a local crisis line — crisis lines talk to children, teenagers and parents too.

sections.h2: The scenario: grow, uproot, start again
paragraphs: Waite calls the Empress the door or gate by which an entrance is obtained into this life, and an image of universal fecundity: a field of corn is ripening in front of her, and beyond there is a fall of water. In the 3-13-10 tail she stands precisely at the entry. So the circle begins not with a problem but with a rise: an idea, a person, a project, a home appears — and you want to grow all of it. Such a person starts out of desire, not duty. People and resources gather quickly around their idea, and the first fruits appear sooner than other people’s.

Then the season changes. There is nothing catastrophic about this; it is how all living things live: a project needs rules and a different scale, falling in love needs agreements, a grown child needs a different distance, a team needs new roles. At such a moment a gardener prunes branches, moves the plant to a bigger pot, thins something out. In the weak version of 3-13-10 a different reflex kicks in: if the old form no longer fits, then everything is over. And the plant is pulled up by the roots.

Then the Wheel turns and a new season comes: a new field, a new idea, a new rise. The person is generous again, grows things fast again — and at the next change of form again puts a full stop where a comma would have done. After a few turns a familiar feeling appears: “everything starts beautifully for me and always ends the same way”. Wen writes of the Wheel as a card under which history repeats itself and the past becomes the future, down to a sense of déjà vu. For this tail, déjà vu is the most accurate signal that the circle has started another turn.

paragraphs.h3: What uprooting looks like, and what repotting looks like

paragraphs: There is neither cowardice nor whim in the left-hand column. There is decisiveness that has mistaken a stage for the whole.

sections.h2: What keeps the circle going: relief that feels like a revelation
paragraphs: Death in position N is the mechanism that makes the repetition stable. Its mature work is to end what has outlived itself and free up space. In the tail this work is overdone: instead of one dry branch, the whole tree goes. And things immediately feel easier. You don’t have to endure the in-between stage, where the old no longer works and the new has not yet taken shape. You don’t have to watch a beautiful beginning turn into a complex system. Relief fixes the circle in place more reliably than any belief. Wen herself links Death with the darker aspects of the Wheel of Fortune: change you don’t control and a transition you resist.

3-13-10 has a second support too, invisible if you look only at the tail’s three numbers. This tail only arises with a matrix centre of 20 — Judgement (how this works is explained in the section on arithmetic). Waite describes Judgement as a response to a call heard from within: something in us sounds a trumpet, and all that is lower rises in response — “almost in a moment, almost in the twinkling of an eye”. Wen calls this card an epiphany: all the evidence is on the table, the judgement has been made.

In our reading, it is this link that explains why the break in 3-13-10 doesn’t look like running away. The person doesn’t slip off into something new, as in the neighbouring tails with the same entry — they pass a verdict. The decision “that’s it, enough” comes all at once, feels like clarity, almost like an awakening, and so seems unconditionally right. Sometimes it really is right. But the feeling of revelation doesn’t prove the verdict correct: the trumpet can sound out of tiredness, too, or out of fear of the transition. Time helps to tell one from the other — more on this in the practical part.

sections.h2: The second trap: numbness after the ending
paragraphs: In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings, the thirteenth card has “end … destruction”, and reversed, “inertia, sleep, lethargy”. A calculated number has no reversed position, but the pair itself is telling: a transition can be failed in two ways — by cutting it off too early, or by getting stuck after the end. In her reading of the reversed card, Wen describes the second option as a plateau: the person feels it is time to move into a new phase and cannot budge.

In 3-13-10, numbness often follows the break. The garden has been uprooted, the field is empty, and a new desire has not yet come. The Empress is the ability to want and to grow, so the empty field is felt especially sharply: a person used to living from one idea to the next suddenly wants nothing. This, apparently, is where the gloomy interpretations of the tail come from.

The Wheel at the root gives a direct answer: winter is a phase, not the end of the garden. “What goes up will come down. What hits bottom will bounce up,” Wen writes of the tenth arcanum. It helps the holder of 3-13-10 to know a simple thing about themselves: emptiness after an ending happens to them, and it passes. It doesn’t have to be filled at once with a new start, and it shouldn’t be taken as the truth about life. If it drags on and grows heavier, that is a reason to talk to a psychologist, not to look for answers in the matrix.

sections.h2: The root task: stay on the wheel instead of jumping off
paragraphs: Position D is the root task the whole circle keeps returning to. Here stands the Wheel of Fortune. Waite sees in it the perpetual motion of the world and the flux of human life, and in the sphinx at the top of the wheel, the equilibrium within this motion. He specifically notes that seating the sphinx on a fixed pedestal above the wheel spoils the symbol: the meaning of the card is stability amidst movement, not apart from it. And one more of his thoughts: behind the turns of the wheel stands not chance but Providence.

For 3-13-10 this is a ready-made statement of the task. You can’t stop the wheel: the Empress will grow things anyway, and what grows will change form anyway. Jumping off at every turn, as the tail’s Death does, is no way out either. The task is to become someone who stays themselves while the forms change: “this form is over, but the story goes on”. Then the experience of the previous round passes into the next one instead of burning up with the old shell.

In practice, the Wheel teaches you to tell phases apart. Any living undertaking has sowing, growth, a plateau, pruning and winter. A plateau is a pause in growth, not its end. Pruning is care for the tree. Winter is not emptiness for ever. A person with 3-13-10 most often mistakes two difficult but ordinary phases for the end — the plateau and the pruning. Learning to name the phase out loud is already half the work.

sections.h2: How to prune instead of uprooting: practice
paragraphs: The ability to put a full stop is a strength of this tail, and there is no need to give it up. The task is narrower: to end stages, not everything at once. Below are six techniques, each answering a specific link in the circle.

What exactly has stopped working? What of what you have created is still valuable? What next form could it move into? If all three questions have concrete answers, the decision looks like pruning. If there is only one answer — “I want this to be gone” — it is most likely relief talking, not clarity.

Before any ending, write down what you are taking with you: skills, people, money, texts, groundwork, conclusions. The Empress does not grow things so that everything burns. If the inventory comes out empty, you are probably leaving too early: the harvest hasn’t been gathered yet.

A decision to end things comes as a revelation, so let it sit. Say it out loud to someone you trust, set a date and come back to it in a few days. Real clarity will survive the pause; a rush of relief usually won’t.
Find the smallest ending that will relieve the tension: close one role, one format, one commitment, one project out of five. Often this is enough for the tree to start growing again.

When a stage really is exhausted, end it completely: say thank you, hand things over, settle debts and agreements, say goodbye. A break leaves things unsaid, and it is exactly from that unsaid that the numbness after the ending grows. A good ending is Death in its mature form: a horseman with a rose on his banner, not an explosion.

When the feeling “this has happened before” appears in a new situation, stop. This is the place where the circle repeats and where it is easiest to break: make at least one move on this turn differently from the previous ones.

sections.h2: Arithmetic and rarity: what sets 3-13-10 apart among the 26 tails
paragraphs: In the Arcana Sense scheme, the tail is calculated like this: D is the reduced sum of the day, month and year arcana, the centre E is the sum of all four, then M = D + E and N = D + M. Any number over 22 is reduced by adding its digits. For 3-13-10 the arithmetic adds up to an almost narrative picture: the Wheel and Judgement give the Empress (10 + 20 = 30, reduced to 3), and the Wheel and the Empress give Death (10 + 3 = 13). Death in the middle is literally the sum of the root and the entry.

This can be read as a hint — as our interpretation, not a rule of the method. Death here is not an outside force that takes away what you created. It is made of two of your own qualities: what you grow, and the fact that every living thing goes through phases. The meeting of growth with a change of season is inevitable; the only choice is whether it becomes pruning or uprooting.

Add the day arcanum (numbers up to 22 are taken as they are; for 23–31, the sum of the digits), the number of the month and the year arcanum (the sum of the digits of the year; if over 22, add the digits again). If you get exactly 10, your tail is 3-13-10. If you get 28, 37, 46 or 55, the Wheel also stands at the bottom of your chart, but the tail is different: 21-4-10. For example, 4 January 1949: 4 + 1 + 5 (1 + 9 + 4 + 9 = 23, then 2 + 3) = 10.

A sum of exactly 10 requires all three terms to be small, so the tail is rare. From 1 January 1900 to the start of October 2026, 149 dates out of 46,298 give it — 0.32%. That makes it the third rarest of the 26 tails the formula produces; only 9-18-9 and 6-14-8 are rarer. The 21-4-10 tail also has the root 10, and it is about 27 times more common.

Two more features follow from this. The 3-13-10 tail only occurs in people born between 1 January and 1 July. And more than half of the matching dates — 88 of 149 — fall in 2000–2024. There are no such dates at all before 1949, and after 1 January 2024 the next one will not come until 4 January 2030.

For those born in 1949, 1958, 1967, 1976, 1985, 1994, 2003, 2012 and 2021 (45 dates of 149), the same numbers 3-13-10 also stand on the relationship line. This is not a doubled force of the tail but two different positions, each with its own reading: the theme “grow it and don’t cut it off” also sounds in the reading of their close relationships.

sections.h2: 3-13-10 in a child: what parents should know
paragraphs: More than half of the dates with this tail fall in the 2000s, 2010s and 2020s. So people often learn about 3-13-10 while calculating a son’s or daughter’s matrix, and immediately stumble on the word “suicide”. Let us repeat the main point: the tail says nothing about a child’s safety and does not predict events. It describes a way of going through transitions that in childhood is only just taking shape.

It might look like this. A child lights up over a club, a sport, a friendship, a project of their own, throws themselves into it generously and with pleasure — and at the first turn (a new coach, a different class, a first serious failure) wants to drop everything for good. In the logic of the tail, this is not a whim but the same Death, only on a child’s scale.

What helps is a middle path between two extremes: don’t force them to hold on to everything, and don’t let them burn everything at once. Agree to “finish the season” before leaving. Ask not “why are you giving up” but “what from this do you want to keep”. Show by your own example how to end things well: say goodbye, say thank you, take your skills with you. The most valuable thing a child with 3-13-10 can take away from childhood is the experience that after one stage ends, they remain the same person, with everything they managed to grow.

If what worries you is not the matrix but what you see in your child’s mood and behaviour, that is a question for real specialists. Call your local emergency number or a local crisis line — crisis lines advise parents too.

sections.h2: Similar triples: how not to confuse 3-13-10
paragraphs: Tails that share one number are easy to take for relatives. But in a tail, what matters is the number’s role, not the number itself, so their scenarios are different.

head: Tail
What it shares with 3-13-10
How it differs
rows: centre 11 instead of 20: the person answers the turn of the wheel not with a break but with an attempt to hold everything through control
the home grows walls, and the person breaks out by force — or takes everyone under control
stops at the threshold: a new start seems more interesting than the plan that is due to come into the world

paragraphs: Against their background, 3-13-10 stands out because it doesn’t run away but ends things: it passes a verdict and puts a final full stop.

The same three numbers also occur elsewhere in the chart — and there they are no longer a karmic tail but the programme of another line, with its own reading. Most often it is the personal talent line: the 3-13-10 triple stands there for people born in March with centre 7, and there are almost three times as many such dates since 1900 (431) as dates with the tail. Less often it is the relationship line (110 dates, 45 of them belonging to holders of the tail themselves). By the formula, this triple never occurs in the money line.

In the Arcana Sense formula there is no such tail as 10-13-3. If you have seen it in someone else’s reading, most likely the same points have simply been written in reverse order — from the outer bottom point to the inner one. Check against your chart: you have the 3-13-10 tail if 3 is at the inner bottom point, 13 in the middle and 10 at the outer bottom point. In the compatibility matrix the numbers are calculated from two dates, and the 3-13-10 triple there describes the couple, not each partner’s personal tail.

sections.h2: The strong version: a gardener who knows the seasons
paragraphs: A worked-through 3-13-10 gives a rare combination: the ability to create living things from scratch, the courage to clear away what has outlived itself without needless regret, and the understanding that both are parts of one long cycle. Such people are good at taking projects and people through transitions: relaunching projects, moving teams to a new format, helping others close a chapter well without losing what mattered most in it. Where others cling to the shell or throw everything away along with it, they know how to repot.

The difference between the weak and the strong version shows after the ending. The weak one leaves relief, an empty field and a vague déjà vu. The strong one leaves a gathered harvest, a clear conclusion and a next move that builds on what has been lived. The Empress grows, Death prunes, the Wheel turns the season, and Judgement at the centre sounds no longer like a verdict but like a call to the next form of life.

For a couple, 3-13-10 is about growing something shared when familiar conditions change. Here the Empress is the entry to the task, Death is its middle, and the Wheel of Fortune is the main task: staying steady as the couple moves from one stage to the next.

faq.a: No. That is a popular label assembled from a literal reading: the Empress is life, Death is death. Waite interprets the thirteenth arcanum as change of form and renewal, and a karmic tail describes a habitual scenario, not events. 3-13-10 is about how a person ends projects and relationships: too abruptly, all at once and with relief.

It is the third rarest of the 26 possible tails: 149 birth dates since 1900, 0.32%. It only arises if the day, month and year arcana add up to exactly 10. That is why all such dates fall between 1 January and 1 July, and more than half of them in 2000–2024.

faq.q: Is the 3-13-10 tail linked to children, pregnancy or motherhood?
faq.a: The Empress is an image of fertility, but neither Waite nor Wen gives any grounds for predicting pregnancy, childlessness or the loss of a child from her. In this tail she means the ability to grow any living undertaking: a project, a relationship, a home, a team. Readings that link 3-13-10 to abortions or “maternal trauma” go beyond what the cards say.

Both tails have the Wheel of Fortune at the root, but their centres differ: for 3-13-10 it is Judgement (20), for 21-4-10 it is Strength (11). Hence their opposite answers to the turn of the wheel: 3-13-10 ends everything too early, 21-4-10 holds on to everything too tightly. 21-4-10 is about 27 times more common.

faq.q: How do I know the tail has been worked through?
faq.a: By what remains after the ending. If after every ending you have a gathered harvest — people, skills, conclusions — and your next step builds on the previous round instead of starting from zero, the scenario is working in its strong version. The second sign is that you can end one stage without destroying the whole project or the whole relationship.

faq.q: Can I get rid of the 3-13-10 karmic tail?
faq.a: The numbers of the chart don’t change: they are calculated from your date of birth. What changes is how the scenario works. The goal is not for the tail to disappear, but for its Death to prune rather than uproot, and for every new turn of the Wheel to begin with the harvest of the last one.

report.h3: A full stop where a comma would do

report.h3: A verdict that feels like an epiphany

A local emergency number or crisis line will help, free of charge and in confidence; crisis lines also talk to children, teenagers and parents. If a life is in danger, the emergency number comes first.
